Quick update from ops after a first pass of logs and telemetry:

- Observations: between 07:40–07:58 we see elevated queue times on priority lane for tenant qx-tenant (avg queue wait jumped from 12ms -> 180ms). There’s a correlated spike in KV cache eviction rate (~8x baseline) and a rise in backend batch formation latency. A handful of long-lived requests (hold time > 2s) look like hot-key requests that pinned slots.
- Hypothesis: simultaneous prefix-prefetch rollout + a small config change to batch sizing for the priority lane led to cache thrash and HOL (head-of-line) blocking. Prefetch increased write churn and reduced effective cache hit rate, which caused more backend fetches and longer batching windows.

Immediate mitigations we triggered at 09:02 PDT (note: actions executed via Dedicated console):
1) Rolled back the priority-lane batch size change to previous stable value.
2) Disabled prefix prefetch for qx-tenant (ttl/backfill remains).
3) Applied short-lived emergency TTL bump for priority keys (60s -> 300s) to reduce eviction churn.
4) Throttled non-critical background prefetch jobs in the region.

Customer impact: p99 dropped from ~650ms to ~220ms within ~8 minutes post-mitigation; 5xx rate fell to baseline after additional in-flight request drains. We attached a short timeline.

Next steps (ops + infra): run targeted replay on staging using qx trace to validate full recovery path and tune prefetch rate limiter. Owner: Ben Carter (ops).

Recommended external message (short): "We saw an internal cache/config interaction that temporarily increased latency and 5xxs. We've rolled back the recent batching and prefetch changes and applied temporary TTL safeguards — latency is recovering and we don't expect further customer impact. We'll follow up with the post-incident summary."

I’ll join a call if Quantix wants a live walk-through and can prepare a post-incident timeline for execs.

—Ben
